title: Acute Pyelonephritis in Pregnancy: Assessment, Admission and Follow-Up

evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant women with suspected acute pyelonephritis in the emergency department (ED), obstetric triage or ward: recognition, sepsis risk, cultures, antibiotic pathway, obstetric monitoring, 48-hour review and suppression. Uses the Saudi Ministry of Health (MOH) urinary tract infection (UTI) protocol, NICE NG111 and NICE NG255; a StatPearls review fills gaps the guidelines leave and is labelled.
findings: Rebuilt from the thin 21 Oct 2026 version: presentation, red flags, diagnostic criteria, six time-ordered management steps, branched medicines (oral, intravenous choose-one, beta-lactam allergy, suppression) and a guideline comparison added.
Saudi MOH and NICE disagree on the first intravenous cephalosporin; both are shown side by side and the Saudi option is marked preferred.
Every dose and threshold traces to a source section opened on 22 Oct 2026.
unverifiedSections: The Saudi MOH protocol lists ceftriaxone and cefazolin without ranking them; ceftriaxone, the first listed, is marked preferred.
Suppression after pyelonephritis is from a review (StatPearls 'may be considered'), not a guideline; it is a specialist decision.
Aztreonam for beta-lactam allergy is from a review only; NICE NG111 gives no non-beta-lactam option in pregnancy.
Distinguishing features listed for each differential are clinical descriptions, not taken from an opened guideline section.
Typical adult reference ranges (white cells, potassium) are not from the cited sources; pregnancy-adjusted local laboratory ranges apply.
Renal (CKD) and hepatic (CLD) lines come from the platform batch-01 table and were not re-opened against each label in this task; nitrofurantoin renal threshold not verified.
SFDA registration of each medicine was not verified (register not reachable from this environment).

pathophysiology.summary: Progesterone relaxes ureteric smooth muscle and the growing uterus compresses the ureters, causing calyceal dilation and urinary stasis that let bladder bacteria ascend to the kidney (StatPearls, Section Etiology). Infection is right-sided in most cases and bilateral in up to 25% (StatPearls, Section Epidemiology). Escherichia coli causes 60–82.5% of cases (StatPearls, Section Etiology). Bacteraemia, sepsis, pulmonary oedema and preterm labour are the main threats (StatPearls, Section Complications).
keyMechanisms: Progesterone lowers ureteric tone; ureters and calyces dilate (StatPearls, Section Etiology).
Uterine compression, vesicoureteric reflux and higher post-void residual cause stasis (StatPearls, Section Etiology).
Right side predominates; bilateral disease in up to 25% (StatPearls, Section Epidemiology).
Escherichia coli 60–82.5%, Klebsiella pneumoniae 11%, Proteus 5% (StatPearls, Section Etiology).
Systemic spread: bacteraemia 7.5%, sepsis 13.3%, septic shock 1.9%; pulmonary oedema or acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) in up to 10% (StatPearls, Section Complications).

symptoms: Flank (loin) pain (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
Fever of 38.0 °C or more with chills (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
Malaise, anorexia, nausea and vomiting (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
Uterine tightening or contractions (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
physicalSigns: Costovertebral angle tenderness (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
Suprapubic or generalised abdominal tenderness (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
Tachycardia and hypotension signal evolving sepsis (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
Cervical change on obstetric assessment (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
redFlags: Heart rate above 130/min (NICE NG255 high-risk criteria).
Respiratory rate 25/min or more, or new need for 40% oxygen or more to keep saturation above 92% (NICE NG255 high-risk criteria).
Systolic blood pressure 90 mmHg or less, or more than 40 mmHg below usual (NICE NG255 high-risk criteria).
New altered mental state; no urine for 18 hours or under 0.5 mL/kg/hour if catheterised; mottled or ashen skin, cyanosis or non-blanching rash (NICE NG255 high-risk criteria).
Contractions or threatened preterm labour (StatPearls, Section Complications).
precipitants: Structural or functional urinary tract abnormality, diabetes or immunosuppression (NICE NG111, Section 1.1 referral).
Recurrent urinary infection in pregnancy, 4–5% of pregnancies (StatPearls, Section Epidemiology).
Pregnancy itself makes any UTI 'complicated' in the Saudi MOH protocol (Saudi MOH UTI protocol, Section Definitions).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Pain migrates to the right iliac fossa or right flank without pyuria; listed as a differential by StatPearls (Section Differential Diagnosis).
Colicky pain with haematuria and little fever; ultrasound shows a stone or obstruction (StatPearls, Section Differential Diagnosis).
Fever with uterine tenderness, often after membrane rupture, and a clean urine (StatPearls, Section Differential Diagnosis).
Constant abdominal pain with a tense uterus and vaginal bleeding or fetal compromise (StatPearls, Section Differential Diagnosis).
Right upper quadrant or epigastric pain; check amylase and lipase (StatPearls, Section Evaluation).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: 10⁵ colony-forming units (CFU)/mL or more of a single organism from a clean-catch sample (StatPearls, Section Evaluation).
Flank pain and fever of 38.0 °C or more with a urinary source, in pregnancy (StatPearls, Section History and Physical).
Any one NICE NG255 high-risk criterion (see Red flags): senior review and intravenous antibiotics within 1 hour (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).

Two or more moderate-high criteria (for example heart rate 100–130/min in pregnancy, respiratory rate 21–24/min, temperature below 36 °C) or systolic blood pressure 91–100 mmHg (NICE NG255 risk evaluation).

clinicalManagement.title: Score sepsis risk
actions: Check NICE NG255 high-risk and moderate-high criteria (see Red flags) (NICE NG255 risk evaluation).
High risk: immediate review by a senior decision maker (ST3 or above) and consultant discussion (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).
Take venous blood gas with glucose and lactate, blood cultures and clotting screen (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).

clinicalManagement.title: Culture, then treat
actions: Send a midstream urine for culture before the first dose (NICE NG111, Section 1.1).
High risk: intravenous antibiotics within 1 hour (NICE NG255 hospital pathway); choose from Medicines.
Moderate-high risk: review by a prescriber within 1 hour; senior review within 3 hours to decide on antibiotics if not escalated (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).

clinicalManagement.title: Fluids and escalation
actions: Lactate above 4 mmol/L or systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg: intravenous fluid bolus within 1 hour and refer to critical care (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).
Lactate 2–4 mmol/L: intravenous fluid bolus within 1 hour (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).
No response within 1 hour of any intervention: alert the consultant (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).
Observations at least every 30 minutes, or continuous in the ED (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).

clinicalManagement.title: Admit with obstetric care
actions: Admit: hospitalisation is usually required (StatPearls, Section Treatment / Management); NICE advises considering referral for every pregnant woman (NICE NG111, Section 1.1).
Obstetric review; after viability, continuous fetal heart rate and contraction monitoring (StatPearls, Section Evaluation).
Give intravenous fluids to maintain urine output (StatPearls, Section Treatment / Management).

clinicalManagement.title: Review at 48 hours
actions: Review the intravenous antibiotic by 48 hours and switch to oral where possible (NICE NG111 visual summary, Table 2).
Change to the culture result, using a narrow-spectrum agent (NICE NG111, Section 1.1).
Worse at any time or not improving by 48 hours: look for another diagnosis, obstruction or abscess — request renal ultrasound (NICE NG111, Section 1.1; StatPearls, Section Evaluation).

clinicalManagement.title: Complete treatment and plan follow-up
actions: Oral cefalexin course is 7–10 days (NICE NG111 visual summary, Table 2); review total intravenous plus oral duration of 7–14 days (StatPearls, Section Treatment / Management) — see Guideline comparison.
Decide with obstetrics or infection whether suppression is needed for the rest of pregnancy (see Medicines).
Relapse or reinfection: refer to the infectious diseases consultant (Saudi MOH UTI protocol, Section General principles).

regimens.indication: Acute pyelonephritis, stable and able to take oral medicine
regimens.patientGroup: Pregnant woman 12 years and over, no sepsis criteria, tolerating oral fluids
regimens.dose: 500 mg; 1–1.5 g per dose for severe infection
regimens.frequency: Twice or three times daily; three or four times daily for severe infection
adjustments: Narrow to the urine culture result when it returns (NICE NG111, Section 1.1).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so Saudi registration was not verified; check the register and the hospital formulary before prescribing.
Paediatric: Not applicable — maternity topic; neonatal care follows the neonatal pathway.

Penicillin allergy: Sources differ: the BNF advises avoiding it only after anaphylaxis or another immediate reaction to a penicillin (or with any cephalosporin allergy) and otherwise allows use with monitoring; some product information (for example ceftriaxone) lists any penicillin hypersensitivity as a contraindication. Alternative: History of anaphylaxis or another immediate reaction to penicillin: avoid cephalosporins and get urgent microbiology advice — NICE NG111 gives no non-beta-lactam option in pregnancy; the aztreonam row in this topic is the review-sourced option (StatPearls).

CKD: creatinine clearance 30–59 mL/min: maximum 1 g/day; 15–29 mL/min: 250 mg every 8–12 h; 5–14 mL/min: 250 mg every 24 h (product label). [batch-01 renal/hepatic table; label not re-opened in this task]
CLD: No dose change. [batch-01 renal/hepatic table; label not re-opened in this task]
monitoring: Temperature, pulse, blood pressure and respiratory rate against the NICE NG255 criteria.
Reassess if symptoms worsen at any time or do not start to improve within 48 hours (NICE NG111, Section 1.1).
contraindications: Cephalosporin allergy, or anaphylaxis/immediate reaction to a penicillin (see Penicillin allergy line).
Any NICE NG255 high-risk criterion: use the intravenous branch.

medicationPlan.note: Choose one branch. In the intravenous branch give one cephalosporin only. Never use fluoroquinolones in pregnancy (Saudi MOH) and never use nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin to treat pyelonephritis (StatPearls). Paediatric, penicillin-allergy, chronic kidney disease (CKD) and chronic liver disease (CLD) lines are on every row; CKD and CLD lines need pharmacist confirmation. SFDA registration not verified.

guidelineComparison.title: Pyelonephritis in pregnancy: where sources differ

values: Ceftriaxone 1–2 g every 24 hours or cefazolin 1 g every 8 hours
Cefuroxime 750 mg–1.5 g three or four times daily
Ceftriaxone or cefepime 1 g every 24 hours; ampicillin plus gentamicin second line
Oral step-down by culture (no named agent)
Cefalexin 500 mg twice or three times daily (1–1.5 g for severe), 7–10 days
Step down after at least 48 hours once afebrile and eating
May be considered: nitrofurantoin 100 mg or cefalexin 250–500 mg daily

guidelineComparison.note: Values are shown as each source states them; none are merged.

learningObjectives: Apply NICE NG255 criteria to grade sepsis risk in pregnancy.
Choose one antibiotic branch and step down by 48 hours.
Recognise obstetric complications that need fetal monitoring.
keyPoints: Culture before the first dose; intravenous antibiotics within 1 hour if high risk.
One cephalosporin only; no fluoroquinolones in pregnancy.
Not better by 48 hours: image the kidneys.
pitfalls: Treating pregnant pyelonephritis as simple cystitis at home.
Using nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin for upper tract infection.
Missing contractions or fetal compromise while focusing on the infection.

patientEducation: Explain the diagnosis, the antibiotic plan and the culture follow-up.
Before discharge give information on sepsis warning signs and how to return (NICE NG255 hospital pathway).
Return at once for fever, worsening flank pain, vomiting that stops tablets, contractions or vaginal bleeding.
lifestyleAndDiet: Keep drinking enough to maintain urine output while unwell (StatPearls, Section Treatment / Management).
mdtReferrals: Critical care if NICE NG255 high-risk criteria persist
Infectious diseases or microbiology for allergy, resistance, relapse or reinfection
Urology if obstruction or abscess on ultrasound
dischargeCriteria: Afebrile and observations normal by NICE NG255 criteria.
Culture result reviewed or a named person will act on it.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Antenatal review after the course; repeat urine culture if symptoms recur; follow any suppression plan agreed by obstetrics or infection.
